name: Pavol Országh Hviezdoslav
credit: Photograph of Pavol Országh Hviezdoslav · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Pavol Országh Hviezdoslav (1849–1921) was the foremost Slovak poet of the nineteenth century. Born in Vyšný Kubín in Orava, he trained in law, worked as a lawyer and judge in northern Slovakia, and wrote under the pen-name Hviezdoslav, 'glory of the stars'.

His long lyrical-epic poems, among them Hájnikova žena (1884–86) and Krvavé sonety (1914), gave Slovak a literary language of unmatched richness and made him the national poet. He also translated Shakespeare, Goethe, Pushkin and Lermontov into Slovak.
